A slow moving thunderstorm complex dropped 2 to 3 inches of rain within an hour, which resulted in major street flooding and the flooding of buildings. One apartment complex in northeast El Paso was evacuated, and several streets were closed. In west El Paso, up to 4 feet of water covered roads at the base of the Franklin Mountains, with many streets in the area closed. Several cars were stuck, and at least one water rescue was performed.
A Skywarn Spotter reported 3 inches of rain within an hour in Chaparral, and the surrounding neighborhood was flooded.

Upslope conditions within a tropical air mass resulted in 6 to 10 inches of rainfall within 6 hours. The area is remote, so the only effects were a ranch under water (according to the rancher) and a couple of highways flooded. Dark Ridge Observatory near Weed reported more than 6 inches of rain from the event.

Two thunderstorms with very heavy rain passed over Truth or Consequences and Elephant Butte. Highways 51 and 195 were closed, and many other streets were impassable. Water entered businesses along  Broadway Street downtown. A 7 foot deep wall of water in Ash Canyon (east of Truth or Consequences) washed out Highway 51 and triggered mudslides.
Highway 9 was flooded east of Columbus.

A large cluster of thunderstorms moved over an area already saturated from heavy rain the previous day. Arroyos overflowed and low water crossings were flooded. Highways that were closed included Highway 9 between Columbus and Hachita, Highway 26 between Deming and Hatch, and Highway 27 south of Hillsboro.

About 3 inches of rain fell within an hour over already-saturated ground in the western portion of Deming. Major street flooding occurred, with most roads closed west of Highway 11. This same area was under 2 to 3 feet of water which entered homes and businesses. Power was out in the majority of the city as water logged power poles were easily knocked over by 45 mph wind gusts.
Heavy rain caused a rock slide on Highway 152 near Emory Pass on the Sierra/Grant County Line.

Rainfall amounts of up to 2 inches fell on the South Tularosa Fire burn scar above Mescalero, resulting in excessive runoff. Logs washed on to Route 10, and much debris blocked residences. A fish hatchery was destroyed which killed all the fish.
Numerous roads were flooded throughout central Luna County according to the Luna County Road Department.
Scattered power and phone lines were down throughout Deming.

The circulation from former Hurricane Dolly passed directly over west El Paso. Rainfall amounts ranged from an inch and a half in eastern El Paso County and extreme western Hudspeth County to well over 3 inches in west El Paso. Trans Mountain Road was closed between Interstate 10 and U.S. Highway 54 due to numerous rock slides. Many roads were flooded and several were closed from Fort Hancock to Anthony.

A thunderstorm formed in the residual moisture from the remnants of Dolly and dropped very heavy rain on northwest El Paso. Streets were flooded over the curb with run-off from the Franklin Mountain slopes mainly north of Redd Road.
The remnants of Dolly brought 2.5 to 3.5 inches of rain to southern Dona Ana County. Water was knee deep in Chaparral, and Highway 28 was flooded south of La Union.
Residual moisture from the remnants of Dolly led to heavy rainfall and flash flooding in the town of Dona Ana. Several roads were barricaded and water entered numerous homes.

Moisture associated with the remnants of Dolly resulted in very heavy rain over the South Tularosa Canyon Fire burn scar. Flood waters over-topped containment ponds leading to a widespread flash flood event. Parts of U.S. 70 were closed, the road to the Mescalero Fire Station was washed out, and numerous secondary roads were closed die to high water. Two dams failed at Mud Canyon. Several buildings were affected by the flood waters.
There were at least 5 road closures throughout the city due to flooding.
Multiple low water crossings were flooded. Other areas were only accessible to four wheel drive vehicles due to excessive debris.

High temperatures on Feb 2nd only warmed to around 19F at Silver City and 23 at the GIla Center RAWS. Low temperatures on the morning of Feb 3rd dropped to -9F at the Silver City Airport, -13F at Mule Creek, and -11F at the Gila Center RAWS.  Natural gas was shut off to many residents around the Silver City area because of low pressure in the lines due to the high demand.

High temperatures across the region on Feb 2nd included 20 at Antelope Wells, and 21 in Lordsburg. Low temperatures on the morning of Feb 3rd included -2F at Antelope Wells, 0F at Animas and 0F at Lordsburg.

High temperatures across the region on Feb 2nd included 16F at Deming and 18F about 10 miles south of Deming. Low temperatures on the morning of Feb 3rd included -3F at Cambray near the Luna/Dona Ana County line on Interstate 10, -1F about 10 miles south of Deming, and 0F at Deming. Numerous frozen and burst water pipes were reported.  The Marshall Memorial Library in Deming was closed for some time due to a break in the building's fire suppression system causing damage to the ceiling and insulation.

High temperatures reported across the area on Feb 2nd included 18F at Las Cruces, 16F in Santa Teresa at the National Weather Service Office, 12F at the White Sands Missile Range Headquarters and 13F at Northrup Landing. Morning low temperatures on Feb 3rd included 0F at Las Cruces, -20F at Jornada, -5F at the National Weather Service in Santa Teresa, -10F at the White Sands Missile Range Headquarters and -15F at Northrup Landing.  Numerous frozen and broken pipes were reported, natural gas pressure was at all-time lows and schools were closed for 4 days due to all the problems caused by the cold.

High temperatures around the area on Feb 2nd included 11F at Truth or Consequences and 18F at Hillsboro. Morning low temperatures on Feb 3rd included -17F on the north end of the Blacks Range, -10F at Hillsboro and -6F at Truth or Consequences.  Each morning from the 1st through the 4th had low temperatures below 10F at Truth or Consequences.

High temperatures across the region on Feb 2nd included 9F at McGregor Range, 16 at Alamogordo and 18 at Orogrande. Low temperatures on the morning of Feb 3rd included -19F at Holloman Air Force Base, -13F at Alamogordo Airport, -11F at Orogrande and -7F at McGregor Range. Six water main breaks were reported in Alamogordo.  Natural gas was shutoff to about 5000 customers in the area. The city of Alamogordo declared an emergency in the city due to the extreme winter weather. Around 4000 residents in the county were without natural gas for several days. Most schools were closed for 3 days due to the cold and lack of water and heat, a couple in Alamogordo were closed for 5 days.

High temperatures across the Sacramento Mountains on Feb 2nd included -4F at Weed, -3F at Mayhill, -1F in Cloudcroft and 1F at Mescalero. Overnight low temperatures on Feb 3rd included -30F at the Inn of the Mountain Gods in Mescalero, -19F in Cloudcroft, -20F at Mayhill, -16F in Weed and -18F at Cosmic. The town of Cloudcroft lost between 500,000 and 600,000 gallons of water due to water line breaks.

High temperatures on Feb 2nd only warmed up to around 15F degrees across all of El Paso County.  This broke the all-time record low high temperature for the city of El Paso. The low temperature on the morning of Feb 3rd fell to around 0F with 1F officially at the El Paso International Airport. El Paso experienced 78 consecutive hours of temperatures at or below freezing. All 8 of El Paso Electrics generators froze causing rolling blackouts across the city for several days. Over 200,000 customers went without electricity for at least part of the day on Feb 3rd. Due to the rolling blackouts...the water pumping stations were not able to pump enough water to keep the reservoirs full. This water problem caused water restrictions and a boil order to be put into effect. Many water main breaks and thousands of pipes in buildings throughout the city burst. Schools were closed for 5 days due to lack of water, electricity and heat.

High temperatures on Feb 2nd only warmed up to 14F in Dell City. Overnight low temperatures on Feb 3rd fell to -5F at Dell City and 2F in Sierra Blanca. All of Northern Hudspeth County from near Hueco Tanks to Dell City lost power for about 12 hours from the evening of Feb 2nd until early morning Feb 3rd.

Through the month of May, the eastern half of Hudspeth County was in Exceptional(D4) drought.  The remainder of Hudspeth County was in Extreme(D3) drought. No measurable precipitation was reported in most areas since early February, and in some cases since late October 2010.

Through the month of May, all of El Paso County was in Extreme(D3) drought. No measurable precipitation was reported at the El Paso International Airport since early February when 0.11 inches was reported. Since October 5th, only 0.29 inches had been reported at the airport. This was the third driest October-May period on record.

All of Sierra County started out in Extreme(D3) drought and by the end of the month, the Exceptional(D4) drought area extended through the eastern half of the county. Only 0.11 inches of precipitation was reported at the Truth or Consequences Airport since October 5th with no precipitation reported in the month of May.

At the beginning of May, the entire area was under Extreme(D3) drought. By the end of the month, the far northeast corner of Dona Ana County was into Exceptional(D4) drought. No precipitation fell in the month of May and the Las Cruces Airport had no received any precipitation since early February.

At the beginning of May, the western areas of the Sacramento Mountains were under Extreme(D3) drought with the eastern slopes in Exceptional(D4) drought. By the end of the month, the entire area was in Exceptional(D4) drought. No precipitation fell in the month of May and the region had received little or no precipitation since early February. The Mayhill Fire occurred from May 9-May 28 and scorched nearly 32,000 acres of land. The Lincoln National Forest was closed May 12th to all visitors and was not opened until middle July.

Throughout the month of May, the entire area was under Extreme(D3) drought. Only 0.13 inches of rain was reported at the Deming Airport since October 5th with no precipitation falling in the month of May.
Throughout the month of May, the entire area was under Extreme(D3) drought.  No precipitation fell in the month of May and little to no precipitation had fallen since the beginning of the year.

The entire area was under Extreme(D3) drought through the month of May. No precipitation fell in the month of May and only 0.10 inches had fallen since the beginning of the year. The Miller Fire started April 28th and lasted through the month of May until June 7th with nearly 90,000 acres burned. This fire closed the Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument for several days.

At the beginning of May, the entire area was under Extreme(D3) drought. By the end of the month, all areas except the far southwest corner of Otero County was into Exceptional(D4) drought. No precipitation fell in the month of May and only 0.06 inches of rain had fallen since October 22nd at the Alamogordo Airport.

The eastern half of Sierra County started out in exceptional(D4) drought with the remainder of the area in extreme(D3) drought. By the end of June, the entire area was in exceptional(D4) drought. The Truth or Consequences airport only received a trace of precipitation in the month. The yearly rainfall through the month of June at the Truth or Consequences airport was only 0.06 inches.

The northeastern corner of Dona Ana County started out in exceptional(D4) drought with the remainder of the area in extreme(D3) drought. By the end of June, the entire area was in exceptional(D4) drought except the far southeast. The COOP at New Mexico State University received 0.35 inches in the month. The yearly rainfall through the month of June at New Mexico State University was only 0.43 inches.

The entire Southern Sacramento Mountains were in exceptional(D4) drought through the month of June. The Cloudcroft COOP received 0.68 inches in the month. The yearly rainfall through the month of June in Cloudcroft was 1.58 inches. Normal rainfall through the month of June is 9.18 inches.

All of Hidalgo County started out in extreme(D3) drought, and by the end of June, the entire area was in exceptional(D4) drought. The Animas COOP only received 0.01 inches of precipitation in the month. The yearly rainfall through the month of June at the Animas COOP was only 0.07 inches.

All of Luna County started out in extreme(D3) drought and by the end of June, the entire area was in exceptional(D4) drought. The Deming airport only received 0.01 inches of precipitation in the month. The yearly rainfall through the month of June at the Deming airport was only 0.03 inches.

All of Otero County except the far southwest portion started out in exceptional(D4) drought and remained there through the month. The Alamogordo airport only received 0.03 inches of precipitation in the month. The yearly rainfall through the month of June at the Alamogordo airport was only 0.09 inches.

All of El Paso County remained in extreme(D3) drought through the month of June. The El Paso airport received 0.05 inches of precipitation during the month.  The yearly precipitation at the El Paso airport was 0.16 inches. The precipitation in the early part of the month broke a stretch of 119 consecutive days without measurable precipitation at the airport.

The western half of Hudspeth County remained in extreme(D3) drought through the month of June while the eastern half was in exceptional(D4) drought. The Fort Hancock COOP received 0.18 inches of precipitation during the month which was the first measurable precipitation recorded there for the year.

Exceptional Drought(D4) conditions continued across all of Sierra County through the month of July. The Truth or Consequences Airport did receive 0.72 inches of rain in the month, but this was the first measurable precipitation since early February with only 0.83 inches recorded since October 5th, 2010.

Most of Dona Ana County was in Exceptional Drought(D4) through the month of July except for the far southeast portion of the county which was in Extreme Drought(D3). |The official observing site at New Mexico State University did receive 2.01 inches of precipitation in the month, but since early October 2010, the total precipitation was only 2.45 inches.  The average yearly precipitation at this site is over 9.5 inches.

Exceptional Drought(D4) conditions continued across all of the Sacramento Mountains through the month of July. The cooperative observer at Mountain Park only received 2.67 inches of rain in the month and the observer at Elk only received 0.79 inches with the yearly total only at 1.42 inches at the end of the month. The average annual precipitation at Elk is over 17 inches.

Exceptional Drought(D4) conditions continued across all of Luna County through the month of July. The Deming Airport did receive 1.00 inches of rain in the month, but this only brought the yearly total up to 1.03 inches. The average annual precipitation is around 9 inches.

Exceptional Drought(D4) conditions continued across all of Hidalgo County through the month of July. The cooperative observer at Antelope Wells did receive 1.88 inches of rain in the month, but this was the first measurable precipitation since December 2010. The average annual precipitation at Antelope Wells is 12.38 inches.

Exceptional Drought(D4) conditions continued across all of the Gila Region through the month of July. The Silver City Airport did receive 1.78 inches of rain in the month, but this only brought the yearly total up to 1.88 inches. The cooperative observer at Redrock received 1.18 inches of rain in the month but only brought the yearly total to 1.42 inches.  The average annual precipitation at Redrock is over 13 inches.

Exceptional Drought(D4) conditions continued across all of the Tularosa Basin and southern desert of Otero County through the month of July except for a small area over far Southwest Otero County which was in Extreme Drought(D3). The Alamogordo Airport did receive 0.54 inches of rain in the month, but this only brought the yearly total up to 0.63 inches. The average annual precipitation is around 13 inches. The cooperative observer in Orogrande did receive 4.11 inches for the month, but only brought the yearly total up to 4.20 inches.  The yearly average precipitation is around 12 inches in Orogrande.

All of El Paso County remained in Extreme(D3) drought through the month of July. The El Paso Airport received 2.59 inches of rain, but that brought the total to only 2.75 inches since early October. Most areas of El Paso County did not receive nearly as much rain as the airport during the month. Average rainfall from October through July is about |eight inches.

The western half of Hudspeth County was in Extreme(D3) drought through the month of July while the eastern half was in Exceptional(D4) drought. The cooperative observer in Fort Hancock received 0.53 inches of rain during the month which brought the yearly total up to only 0.71 inches. The average yearly rainfall at Fort Hancock is about 9.5 inches.

The drought severity for El Paso County dropped to Severe(D2) at the beginning of August with only the extreme western areas of the county remaining in the severe category at the end of the month.  The remainder of the county was downgraded to Moderate(D1) drought on August 9th. Rainfall total for the El Paso Airport in August was 1.11 inches which brought the area to slightly below normal precipitation for the year.

Hudspeth County start out the month of August in Exceptional(D4) drought across the far eastern areas and down to Severe(D2) drought in the far west. By the end of the month, the far western quarter of the county was rated in Moderate(D1) drought while the remainder of the county changed very little. The cooperative observer in Fort Hancock reported 1.60 inches of rain for the month of August.

All of Sierra County was in Exceptional(D4) drought at the beginning of the month and the whole county was in Extreme(D3) drought at the end. The Truth or Consequences Airport received 1.92 inches of rain during the month which brought their yearly total up to 2.70 inches. Normal precipitation for the year through August is around 5 inches.

All of Dona Ana County was in Exceptional(D4) drought except for the far southeast corner which was mainly in Extreme(D3) drought to start the month. At the end of the month, all the areas that were in Exceptional drought were in Extreme(D3) drought with the extreme southeast corner of the county in Severe(D2) drought. The cooperative observer at New Mexico State University received 1.38 inches of rain in August which brought the yearly total up to 3.82 inches.  The normal yearly precipitation through August is around 6 inches.

The entire Southern Sacramento Mountains zone remained in Exceptional(D4) drought through the month of August. The cooperative observer in Elk reported 0.97 inches of rain for the month which brought the yearly total up to 2.39 inches. Normal yearly precipitation through the month of August is around 12 inches.

All of Luna County was in Exceptional(D4) drought at the beginning of August with the whole county at Extreme(D3) drought at the end of the month. The Deming Airport reported 1.29 inches of rain in the month which brought the yearly total up to 2.32 inches. Normal precipitation through August at Deming is just over 6 inches.

The entire area was in Exceptional(D4) drought at the beginning of the month and all areas except the far eastern part of the bootheel, which was in Extreme(D3) drought, remained in the Exceptional(D4) category. The cooperative observer in Antelope Wells received 1.86 inches of rain in the month which brought the yearly total up to 3.74 inches. Normal yearly precipitation through August is almost 9 inches.

The entire area was in Exceptional(D4) drought at the beginning of August and was in Extreme(D3) drought at the end of the month. The cooperative observer at Redrock reported 0.93 inches or rain during the month which brought the yearly total up to 2.35 inches. The normal yearly precipitation through August is over 8.5 inches.

Except for the far southwestern portions of Otero County which was in Extreme(D3) drought, the remainder of the Otero County plains were in Exceptional(D4) drought to start the month. By the end of August, the Extreme(D3) conditions extended from the far southwest corner of the county up through extreme western Otero County. The remainder of the area remained in Exceptional(D4) drought. The Alamogordo Airport reported only 0.19 inches of rain for the month which brought the yearly total up to 0.82 inches.

Numerous water rescues were reported with the worst location in east El Paso near the intersection of Fierro and Bywood where 2 people were pulled to safety. ||Cars were stalled at North Mesa Street near the University of El Paso. Other areas where cars were stalled included the intersections of Cotton and Missouri as well as Gold Avenue and Elm Street. ||Several other major intersections in El Paso were closed by 1030pm including Montwood and Wedgewood, McRae and Gateway East, Montana and Piedras, Yarbrough and Montwood, and Hawkins and North Loop. ||Trans Mountain Road was closed due to flooding, heavy rain and poor visibility.

Interstate 10 remained closed until approximately 1am mst. Through the duration of the event, the El Paso Fire Department responded to 135 incidents which included stalled cars, over 50 water rescues, electric hazards and flooding at houses. ||Rainfall totals from the evening of the 17th to the early morning of the 18th included 3.11 inches within an hour in the Eastwood(Album) Park area on the east side.

The Sierra County Newspaper reported Canal Road at Trujillo Creek was closed by the Arrey Fire Department due to flooding.  The Little Greenhorn Creek was also flooding onto Highway 187 south of the Hillsboro Interstate 25 exit.

Grant County 911 reported a flash flood near Bear Creek off of Highway 211. A Chevrolet Prism was pushed off the road and into the creek on Highway 211. The woman was able to escape her vehicle and get to safety, but the vehicle was found a half mile down from the highway in a wash and was totaled.

Very heavy rain occurred over northeast and central El Paso with over 5 inches of rain reported in about 4 hours. Several water rescues were reported including at the intersection of Alcan and Fairbanks. Another water rescue was attempted at Vulcan and Diana but resulted in a fatality of a 64 year old woman. ||Interstate 10 West at the Cotton exit ramp was closed, Dyer Street between Diana and Manila was closed as well as Scenic Drive due to flooding.

Interstate 10 remained closed through approximately 930am mst. Additional roads were closed around central and northeastern El Paso County including Railroad and Diana along with Joe Herrera Drive. Total rainfall from the storm in northeast El Paso was 6.50 inches at the El Paso Museum of Archeology.
The Truth or Consequences Herald reported that Highway 187 between mile markers 15 and 23 was impassable.

Dona Ana 911 reported numerous roads flooded around Las Cruces including the intersection of Park Hill Drive and Del Rey. A storm survey performed by the office confirmed about 8 houses which had water run through them, fences knocked down and roads washed out around Rocky Canyon Trail and Shalem Colony Trail area. One of the houses had water up to 3 feet deep inside. Reports of over 2 inches of rain in less than 30 minutes were received around the Dona Ana and extreme north Las Cruces areas.
Numerous roads in Truth or Consequences were flooded as well as the Animas Creek. No water made it into the stores around the downtown area however.
Highway 82 was closed just west of the tunnel to Cloudcroft was closed due to a rock slide. A section of road at La Luz Creek crossing was closed as well due to flooding.
The entire zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the month of October. The Cooperative Observer at Gila Hot Springs reported 1.56 inches of rain which was 0.08 inches above normal.
Severe(D2) drought continued to be reported for the northern portion of the zone.

The northern and eastern portions of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the month of October. The Redrock Cooperative Observer reported 0.85 inches of precipitation which was 0.18 inches below normal.

The southwestern up to the northeastern portions of the zone started in Severe(D2) drought but were put into Moderate(D1) drought on October 21st. The Cooperative Observer at Antelope Wells reported 0.61 inches of precipitation which was 0.01 inches below normal.
The eastern portions of the zone started the month in Severe(D2) drought but on October 21st were placed in Moderate(D1) drought.
The entire zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the month of November. The Gila Hot Springs Cooperative Observer reported 0.48 inches of precipitation which was 0.39 inches below normal.
The northern half of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the entire month of November.

The northern and eastern portions of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the month of November. The Redrock Cooperative Observer reported 0.55 inches of precipitation which was 0.11 inches below normal.

A mesonet site located 6 miles north-northwest of El Paso recorded a peak gust of 63 mph. Other peak gusts included 62 mph 8 miles north-northwest of El Paso and 58 mph 5 miles north-northwest of El Paso.

Severe(D2) drought conditions continued across the region during the month of December. The Gila Hot Springs Cooperative Observer reported 1.00 inches of precipitation which was 0.30 inches below normal.
The northern half of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the month of December.
Northern and eastern portions of the zone continued through the month of December. The Redrock Cooperative Observer reported 0.76 inches of precipitation which was 0.25 inches below normal.
The entire zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the month of January. The Gila Hot Springs Cooperative Observer reported 2.21 inches of precipitation which was 1.27 inches above normal.
The northern half of the zone was in Severe(D2) drought during the month of January.

The northern and eastern portions of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought during the month of January. The Redrock Cooperative Observer reported 2.51 inches of precipitation which was 1.65 inches above normal.
A trained spotter in Mule Creek reported 10 inches of snow and a Cooperative Observer reported 7 inches in Gila Hot Springs.

The heaviest snow occurred at Pinos Altos where 11 inches of snow was reported by the Grant County Emergency Manager. Other reports around the zone included 5 inches at Tyrone, 2 miles west-southwest of White Signal and Poverty Creek.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported 5.3 inches of snow about 4 miles north of Akela.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported 5 inches of snow in 5 miles northwest of Las Cruces. Several other observers reported over 4 inches across the city of Las Cruces.

A Cooperative Observer in Sacramento reported 9 inches of snowfall. A CoCoRaHS Observer 5 miles northeast of Cloudcroft reported 7.4 inches of snow with the town of Cloudcroft receiving 7.0 inches of snow.
A CoCoRaHS Observer reported 8.2 inches of snow 16 miles northwest of Las Cruces.
A CoCoRaHS Observer near the foothills of the Franklin Mountains reported 6 inches of snow. Numerous other reports of 4 to 5 inches were received in the same general area.
The northern portions of the zone which started in Severe(D2) drought improved to Moderate(D1) drought on February 3rd.

The zone started with the northern and eastern portions in Severe(D2) drought which was put into Moderate(D1) drought on February 3rd. The remainder of the zone was in Moderate(D1) or Abnormally Dry(D0) drought conditions through the month.

Severe(D2) drought conditions across the entire zone improved to Moderate(D1) conditions over the eastern half of the zone on February 3rd. The Gila Hot Springs Cooperative Observer reported 0.46 inches of precipitation which was 0.41 inches below normal.
KTCS ASOS reported a peak wind of 67 mph from a downdraft associated with weak convective showers in the area.
Severe(D2) drought continued for the western half of the zone in March. The Gila Hot Springs Cooperative Observer reported 0.83 inches of precipitation which was 0.05 inches above normal.

The far western portion of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought for the month of April. The Gila Hot Springs Cooperative Observer reported 0.30 inches of precipitation which was 0.13 inches below normal.
The person that reported golf ball size hail in Weed said it appeared to be more extensive toward the town of Sacramento.
TXDOT out of Dell City reported 1 foot of water on highway 1437 two miles south of town.
The far western portions of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the month of May.
Three large trees were blown down on the NMSU campus at the married housing units.
A 35 foot pine tree was blown down at intersection of Trawood and George Dieter.
The western portion of the zone remained in Severe(D2) drought through the entire month of June.

The ASOS at El Paso International Airport reported a peak gust of 62 mph. Other peak wind gusts included 64 mph 6 miles north-northeast of El Paso and 71 mph 6 miles north of Fort Bliss. In addition, street lights were blown down at Martin Luther King Drive and Jon Cunningham.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES SACRAMENTO MOUNTAINS BELOW 7500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The northern areas of the zone were in Severe(D2) drought while the southern portions were in Moderate(D1) drought. The Mountain Park Cooperative Observer reported 0.20 inches of precipitation which was 1.35 inches below normal.
Three tractor trailers and 1 horse trailer were overturned.
Lemon sized hail reported along with damaging winds.
Highway 52 near Winston was closed due to flooding at the low water crossings.
Pea to nickel sized hail accumulated 1 inch deep.
Water from Poverty Creek rapidly rising and crossing Highway 52 with a depth of 2 to 3 feet.
Water crossing highway 52 to a depth of 2.5 feet. Also pea sized hail.
Traffic was stopped on Highway 11 south of Deming due to intense nickel size hail.
Several trees were blown down and at least one roof blown off in southern portions of Deming. Power poles and lines also down which cutoff power to Columbus.
Stirrup Road was closed east of Deming due to water flowing over the road.
Highway 92 had wash outs from mile marker 0 to mile marker 11.
Big tree limbs were blown off trees.
Quarter sized hail near Canutillo High School.

Flooded streets east of Interstate 10 and south of Trans-Mountains Road. Cars were stalled at the intersection of Resler and Paseo Del Norte. There was also people trapped in a vehicle at Doniphan and Montoya.
Fire Official reported that the Sacramento River was over its banks at the Timberon Lodge. Heavy rain was still occurring and streets were flooding in Timberon.
Water was crossing Riata Road west of U.S. 54. Rain had fallen several hours earlier up near La Luz and flowed down toward Alamogordo.

A video of a tornado west of Ruidoso received a lot of social media attention.  The tornado was located in front of Sierra Blanca Peak around 9000 ft in elevation. No damage or injuries were reported.
Fire department sent water rescue teams out for areas along Interstate 10 from around Bassett Center to Zaragoza. Gateway West was closed from Airway to Geronimo.

Rainfall amounts of 2 to over 3 inches were reported around Alamogordo with multiple road closures put into place. Water was across several roads 6 to 8 inches deep. Winds of up to 50 mph also occurred with the storm.
A spotter estimated wind gusts to 60 mph. Several branches were down on College Avenue between NM-90 and the WNMU Campus, including College and Pope.
Winds blew a fence down in Tularosa. An inch of rain also fell in about 20 minutes with the storm.

Storm survey revealed numerous boats damaged at Marina Del Sur on the south end of Elephant Butte Lake. A couple of metal roofs covering the boats were torn off and/or collapsed and concrete slabs anchoring down the structures were pulled out of the water. An eyewitness described a downburst lasting 15 minutes with torrential rainfall and zero visibility. Property damage was in excess of $1 million.
A retractable roof became airborne and landed on the roof of a trailer and caused it to become punched-in. An anemometer near the damaged site recorded a peak wind of 65 mph.
The Silver City AWOS recorded a peak gust of 61 mph along with rain totaling 2.96 inches over a 2 hour period.
The far western areas of Grant County were dropped from Severe(D2) to Moderate(D1) drought conditions in the middle of the month.
Power poles down in Animas.
Golf ball hail reported near Sonoma Ranch Golf Course.
Mainly quarter size, but some stones were up to golf ball size.
Ping pong ball sized hail reported near Mountain View Hospital in Las Cruces.
Numerous cars and homes damaged. Sky lights broken.
Nickel sized hail was reported near Fort Bliss.
Near Kanozo Road in Horizon City.
Love's Truck Stop in Sparks off I-10.
Hail fell in Oliver Lee State Park.
Landspout tornado reported just south of Separ.
Golf Ball sized hail was reported near mile marker 95 along Interstate 10.
Up to an inch accumulation of hail on County Road 549.
Hail started accumulating on the ground.
Penny size hail at Redd Rd and Resler.
Hail reported at Diana and US 54.
Hail covered the ground from US 54 and Diana to Sun Valley.
Roof blown off mobile home and storage unit blown off the ground.
Quarter size hail 6 blocks north of NMSU.
Hail occurred at New Mexico State University.
Pea to quarter size hail just west of Las Cruces.
Large accumulation of up to quarter size hail on Highway 26 about 9 miles northeast of Deming.
Dime to nickel size hail accumulated on Highway 11 south of Deming.
Up to ping pong ball size hail on Interstate 10 about 3 miles east-southeast of Separ.
Arroyo overflowed from heavy rain. There was a water rescue from a flooded vehicle in Dona Ana.
Flooding reported along Resler between Loop 375 and Redd Road.
Flooding around US 54 and Montana in Central El Paso.
Flooding occurred near Hawkins and Viscount.
Flooding occurred around Hawkins and Viscount.
Measured by contract observers at the El Paso Airport.

Wind gusts up to 76 mph were reported about 5 miles south of Organ. Other reports across the zone included 60 mph at Dripping Springs and 58 mph at the Las Cruces Airport. A sign at Big 5 Sporting Goods was damaged by the wind as well and a piece landed on a customer's head which lead to that person being transported to the hospital.
The Northrup Strip Mesonet site reported a peak gust of 63 mph at 130pm.

A peak gust of 97 mph occurred at San Augustin Pass. Other peak wind gusts across the zone included 65 mph five miles northeast of San Augustin Pass, 63 mph six miles east-southeast of the White Sands Missile Range Main Post, 61 mph at the Main Post, and 69 mph at Condron Field.
A peak gust of 66 mph was reported one mile south of Sunspot. Another mesonet site in Sunspot reported a peak gust of 65 mph.
A mesonet site 15 miles south-southwest of Hachita reported a peak gust of 60 mph.

A peak gust of 61 mph was reported at the El Paso International Airport. Three semis were overturned due to the high winds across El Paso between 315 pm and 6 pm. The first occurred at U.S. 54 and Interstate 10 when the bed of a truck ended up resting on the shoulder of the ramp. Around 5 pm another semi was turned on its side at Transmountain Road and U.S. 54 in northeast El Paso. A third semi was turned on its side on U.S. 54 and Montana.
Snowfall accumulations ranged from 6 inches 7 miles east of Cloudcroft to 13.5 inches in Sunspot. The town of Cloudcroft received 9 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES SACRAMENTO MOUNTAINS BELOW 7500 FEET
events.event_narrative: An observer reported 6 inches of snow 5 miles west of Cloudcroft.
Snowfall amounts across Luna County ranged from 4 to 8 inches with the highest report coming from 11 miles south-southeast of Deming.

A wide range of snowfall totals were reported across Southern Dona Ana County. The greatest accumulation was reported in Organ where 13 inches of snow fell. The National Weather Service Office reported 10.4 inches, while most other areas received 4 to 8 inches including Las Cruces.

Snowfall amounts across the Gila region varied greatly. The greatest reported accumulation was 11.5 inches in Kingston and around 4 to 5 inches around Tyrone and White Signal. Most other locations across the zone received 1 to 4 inches of snow.
An observer in Hillsboro reported a total snow accumulation of 4 inches.

Snowfall totals from Cloudcroft to Sunspot ranged from 15 to 30 inches for the duration of the event. Drifts were much higher as east winds of 80 to 90 mph were also reported during the storm at Sunspot and Apache Point. Numerous trees and power lines were downed along the Sunspot Highway south of Sunspot with power being reported out for several days after.
A couple of reports north of Interstate 10 near the Grant-Hidalgo County line ranged from 4 to 5 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES SACRAMENTO MOUNTAINS BELOW 7500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The Mountain Park Cooperative Observer reported 8 inches of snow. In addition to the snow, Timberon lost power due to strong winds and downed power lines for 3 days and later on Dec 29th, ran out of water.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES SACRAMENTO MOUNTAINS BELOW 7500 FEET
events.event_narrative: A COOP Observer near Elk reported 17 inches of snow over a day and a half.
A solid 6 to 10 inches were reported from all of the CoCoRaHS observers across Western El Paso County.

Total snowfall accumulations over the zone ranged from 5 to 10 inches with the El Paso Airport officially reporting 8.1 inches. The 10 inches was reported on the southeast side of the Franklin Mountains.
An observer in Sierra Blanca reported 9 inches of snow with up to 2 foot drifts.
Snowfall amounts ranged from 2 to almost 5 inches with the maximum report of 4.6 inches 4 miles northwest of Silver City. White Signal reported 4.5 inches.

A peak gust of 72 mph was reported at Salinas Peak. Other reports of high winds included 63 mph twenty miles west-northwest of Tularosa,  60 mph eleven miles southwest of Northrup Strip, 67 mph at Northrup Strip and 60 mph nineteen miles west-northwest of Tularosa.

A peak gust of 95 mph was reported at San Augustin Pass. Other strong wind reports included 64 mph eighteen miles northeast of White Sands Missile Range Main Post and 77 mph five miles northeast of San Augustin Pass.
A peak gust of 60 mph was reported three miles northeast of Rodeo.
Reports from Silver City to Bayard ranged from 3 inches to a maximum of 6.1 inches which occurred 3 miles southwest of Silver City.
A peak wind gust was reported at Salinas Peak. Other wind gusts recorded included 69 mph at Northrup Strip and 61 mph sixteen miles north-northwest of Northrup Strip.

A peak gust of 78 mph was recorded at San Augustin Pass.  Other wind gusts across the zone included 72 mph one mile southeast of the White Sands Main Post, 66 mph at Condron Field and 66 mph 18 miles northeast of White Sands Main Post.
A peak gust of 61 mph was reported about 6 miles northeast of Road Forks.
A peak wind gust of 59 mph was reported 5 miles northeast of downtown El Paso. A peak gust of 58 mph was recorded 10 miles north-northeast of El Paso at 3 am on March 23rd.
A peak wind gust of 85 mph was reported at San Augustin Pass. Other reported gusts included 73 mph at Emre on the White Sands Missile Range and 62 mph at the White Sands Missile Range Museum.
Largest stones were three-quarters of an inch in diameter.
Dime to 1 inch hail was reported around Leasburg.
Quarter sized hail was falling in sheets at the NMSU bookstore.
Half inch to dime size hail fell at the intersection of Carver Road and Turtle Creek Avenue.
Quarter sized hail was completely covering the ground.
Pictures were passed along on Facebook of roof damage from a likely microburst.
A peak wind gust of 67 mph was reported at the Northrup Landing mesonet site.
Dime to nickel sized hail reported just south-southeast of Cloudcroft.
Power lines down at Gateway and Hawkins.
Power lines down at Gateway and Yarbrough.
Trees down at Copia and Alameda.
Numerous roads impassable in and around Silver City. Ridge Road also closed along San Vicente arroyo west of Grant County Airport.

Road damage occurred from flash flooding in Leasburg Dam State Park.  Water made it into park buildings with over a foot of standing water in the Maintenance yard.  Daily rainfall from afternoon and overnight rains totaled 4.04 inches.
Flash flooding reported along Alvarez Road with mud and debris across road.
Thunderstorm winds blew off a 190 foot long horse barn roof.
One day rainfall total of 3.83 inches.
One day rainfall total of 2.08 inches.
Water from Animas Creek was flowing over Capaz Road making it impassable.
Motorists encountered half dollar sized hail about 2 miles west of the U.S. Border Patrol check point.
Video from Manhattan Heights showed cars barely making it through deep, fast-moving water.
Blackfoot Road and 5th Street in Fort Hancock were closed due to water running like a river through them.
Cars and homes were reported flooded along Dick Mayers Dr between Victor Lopez and Chelita drives in east El Paso.
Montwood Drive was closed in both directions near Lake Omega Drive due to flooded roads.
Significant street and stream flooding was reported throughout downtown Silver City.
A landspout tornado was photographed just northwest of Lordsburg.  No damage was reported and no survey was done to rate the tornado. Location and path are approximate based on photographer location.
Four feet of water was in Tularosa creek at a low water crossing on Railroad Drive near Tularosa causing the road to be closed.
Cuchillo Creek overflowed and flooded Highway 52 in Winston.  Water was up to 2 feet deep across the highway.
A RAWS site 28 miles east-northeast of Orogrande reported a peak gust of 64 mph at 537 AM.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES SACRAMENTO MOUNTAINS BELOW 7500 FEET
events.event_narrative: A peak gust of 61 mph was reported 1 mile southwest of High Rolls.
A peak gust of 59 mph was reported at two locations about 8 miles northwest of downtown El Paso.
Hail was up to 2 inches deep.
Quarter size hail in Palomas Canyon.

Numerous reports of flash flooding were received around a 5 mile radius of Williamsburg. Flooding was reported on King Canyon Road and water was above bridge level on Highway 187 along with debris on the road. Palomas Creek was flooded about 6 miles northwest of the I-25 bridge.
Flash flooding was reported across Highway 142 in Monticello.
A 3 hour rainfall total of 4.50 inches was reported in Bayard.

Numerous roads were closed along and near Highway 180 in Silver City due to flash flooding.  Other cities affected by the flooding included  Santa Clara around Twin Sisters Peak Road and numerous roads around Bayard and Hurley.  Rainfall amounts around this area averaged 1 to 2 inches in a couple of hours with a maximum of 4.50 inches in Bayard.
Highway 187 at mile marker 35 south of Williamsburg was closed due to flash flooding.
Water and debris were flowing across Highways 52 and 59.  Hermosa Road was also closed.
Numerous cars damaged along Highway 180 near Highway 61 exit.  Hail covering the ground.
Hail covered the ground.

Supercell thunderstorms (very rare for November in this area) affected much of El Paso. The strongest, which actually weakened before moving into the United States, produced golf ball hail over far east El Paso into Horizon City.  This caused record breaking insurance claims for a single hail event with a total of $200 million damage to vehicles and $100 million to homes. This doubled the previous record from 9-16-09. Flooding also occurred due to excessive hail amounts plugging up drains.
All the low water crossings south of Hillsboro were flowing across Highway 27.
Hail reported at the Cornudas Cafe.  Hail fell for 10 minutes.
Peak winds across the zone included 89 mph at Northrup Strip, 61 mph 19 miles west-northwest of Tularosa and 67 mph 22 miles northwest of Tularosa.

A peak gust of 110 mph was reported at San Augustin Pass.  Other wind gusts across the zone included 88 mph near the White Sands Missile Range Main Post, 80 mph at Condron Field and 6 miles east-southeast of the Main Post and 60 mph 11 miles northeast of Organ.
A peak gust of 85 mph was reported 11 miles southwest of Northrup Strip.
A peak gust of 81 mph was reported 15 miles south-southwest of Hachita.  A 58 mph gust was reported 3 miles northeast of Rodeo.
A mesonet site 5 miles northeast of Road Forks recorded a peak gust of 61 mph.

A peak wind gust of 73 mph was reported 1 mile south of Sunspot.  Other gusts included 67 mph in Cloudcroft and 64 mph in Sunspot. The fire chief in Cloudcroft reported numerous power outages and trees down in the Sacramento Mountains.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES SACRAMENTO MOUNTAINS BELOW 7500 FEET
events.event_narrative: A peak gust of 67 mph was reported 1 mile southwest of High Rolls.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES SACRAMENTO MOUNTAINS BELOW 7500 FEET
events.event_narrative: A peak gust of 58 mph was reported 11 miles northeast of Mescalero.

A peak gust of 71 mph was reported 10 miles north-northeast of EL Paso.  Other reports included 69 mph 5 miles northeast of El Paso, 67 mph 13 miles northeast of El Paso, 62 mph as Ascarate Park and 61 mph at the El Paso International Airport. Reports of winds over 70 mph blew in some french doors including damaging pins and dead bolt near Lee Trevino and Montwood.  Numerous other reports were received of car windows being blown out and trees down.
A 58 mph gust was reported 1 miles south-southeast of Sierra Blanca.
Quarter sized hail covered the ground in Alamogordo.
Some damage to vehicles caused by hail slightly smaller than golf balls.

New Mexico 154 was closed between Rincon and Hatch due to flooding at two low water crossings.  One crossing was located right at mile marker 3 with the other located about 0.7 miles east.  The worst of the flooding was around 4 AM when water ran 3 to 4 feet deep.
Fifteen inches of snow was reported at the McKnight Cabin SNOTEL. The Lookout Mountain SNOTEL reported 10 inches of snow.
An observer 1 mile southeast of Cloudcroft reported 6.5 inches of snow through the day. Additional amounts around the Cloudcroft area ranged from 4 to 7.5 inches.

A foot of snow was reported at the Signal Peak SNOTEL.  Additional snowfall reports across the zone included 11 inches of McKnight Cabin and Copperas Vista, 9 inches at Lookout Mountain, 8 inches at Pinos Altos and 6 inches 1 mile east-northeast of Fort Bayard. Lesser amounts of snow were reported below 7000 feet with 6.2 inches 5 miles northeast of Silver City, 5.5 inches 9 miles east of Hanover and 4.5 inches 4 miles northwest of Silver City.
An observer 2 miles southwest of Cloudcroft reported 9.5 inches of snow with 6.5 inches in Cloudcroft and 6.0 inches 1 miles southeast of Cloudcroft.
A peak gust of 88 mph was recorded at San Augustin Pass.  Other strong wind reports included 71 mph 5 miles northeast of San Augustin Pass and 68 mph at Condron Field.

A Mesonet site at Twin Peaks near Las Cruces reported a peak gust of 68 mph. Other gusts included 64 mph 6 miles west-southwest of Las Cruces, 61 mph at the Las Cruces Airport AWOS, 61 mph at the National Weather Service Office in Santa Teresa and 60 mph 2 miles east-southeast of Talavera.
A peak gust of 65 mph was reported 1 mile southeast of the White Sands Missile Range Main Post.  Other gusts included 61 mph 6 miles east-southeast of the WSMR Main Post, and 60 mph at the Main Post.

The ASOS at the El Paso Airport recorded a peak gust of 69 mph.  Other strong gusts included 68 mph 13 miles north-northeast of El Paso, 64 mph at the house of an NWS employee near Cohen Stadium, 60 mph 3 miles east of El Paso, and 59 mph 13 miles north-northeast of El Paso.
A peak gust of 64 mph was reported 1 mile south-southeast of Sierra Blanca.
A peak gust of 60 mph was recorded about 1 mile north of Dell City.

A peak gust of 68 mph was reported at the Dripping Springs RAWS.  Other peak gusts around the area included 65 mph 2 miles east-southeast of Talavera and 61 mph 10 miles northeast of Las Cruces and also at Twin Peaks.
A peak gust of 65 mph was recorded by the White Sands Missile Range at San Augustin Pass.
A peak wind gust of 68 mph was reported at the Northrup Strip site on the White Sands Missile Range.  A peak gust of 59 mph was also reported at Condron Field on the range.
A Mesonet site at Twin Peaks just east of Las Cruces reported a peak gust of 66 mph.

The Mesonet site at San Augustin Pass by the White Sands Missile Range recorded a peak gust of 81 mph. Other gusts across the zone included 69 mph 1 miles southeast of the White Sands Main Post and 59 mph about 5 miles northeast of San Augustin Pass.
The El Paso International Airport ASOS recorded a peak gust of 58 mph.

A peak gust of 82 mph was reported at San Augustin Pass. Other wind reports across the zone included 70 mph 1 mile southeast of the White Sands Main Post, 64 mph 5 miles northeast of San Augustin Pass and 18 miles northeast of the White Sands Main Post and 59 mph at the White Sands Main Post.

A mesonet site just northeast of Las Cruces reported a peak gust of 74 mph.  A 59 mph gust was recorded at the National Weather Service Office in Santa Teresa, NM and a 58 mph gust was reported at the Las Cruces Airport and at Dripping Springs.
A peak gust of 61 mph was recorded at a mesonet site 16 miles northwest of Northrup Strip. A gust of 59 mph was also recorded 19 miles west-northwest of Tularosa.
A peak gust of 65 mph was recorded 5 miles northeast of Road Forks.
A peak gust of 62 mph was recorded 6 miles northeast of El Paso. The El Paso Airport reported a peak gust of 61 mph with 58 mph gusts recorded 13 miles north-northeast and 3 miles east of El Paso.

events.cz_name: RIO GRANDE VALLEY OF EASTERN EL PASO/WESTERN HUDSPETH COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: A peak gust of 62 mph was recorded at a mesonet site in Fort Hancock.
Hail damage was reported to vehicle windshields on Highway 54 around mile marker 76.
Submerged vehicle reported in low water crossing just northwest of Tularosa on Railroad Avenue in a low water crossing.

Hail from 1.5 inches to 2.5 inches in diameter was reported in and around Sierra Blanca. Some areas had hail up to 3 inches deep. Numerous house windows and automobile windshields were damaged, with many cars left dented. Hail also severely damaged dozens of roofs and even penetrated a few.

A peak gust of 87 mph was reported at San Augustin Pass.  Other peak gusts included 61 mph one mile southeast of White Sands Missile Range Main Post and 60 mph five miles northeast of San Augustin Pass.
A peak gust of 72 mph was reported at the Twin Peaks Mesonet site just northeast of Las Cruces.
A peak gust of 60 mph was reported 5 miles northeast of downtown El Paso.
A 63 mph gust was reported at the Jornada Range mesonet site.
A peak gust of 65 mph was reported at two mesonet sites loacated 19 miles west-northwest of Tularosa and 22 miles northwest of Tularosa.
A RAWS site located 28 miles east-northeast of Orogrande reported a peak gust of 59 mph.
A 58 mph gust was recorded on a Weather Underground site located 1 mile south of Sunspot.
A peak gust of 59 mph was recorded 5 miles northeast of El Paso and the El Paso Airport ASOS recorded a gust of 58 mph.
The Alamogordo ASOS recorded a peak gust of 60 mph.
Water rushing over the curbs and into yards in Canutillo.
Wind gust measured at San Augustin Pass.
Hail reported at the White Sands Missile Range Main Post.
Quarter sized hail and very heavy rain along with high winds near Sierra/Socorro County line.
Spotter 5 miles south-southwest of Hueco Tanks reported power out and pea size hail.
Spotter reported water 4 feet deep crossing Highway 52 at the low water crossing in Winston.
Reported at Border Patrol checkpoint.

Near zero visibilities between mile markers 10 and 12 on Interstate 10 east caused a 4 car pileup.  One of the passengers from the initial crash got out of vehicle, and was struck by another vehicle and died.  Three others involved in the crash were also injured.

Flooding was reported along Rio Vista, Coker and Thunder Roads in Socorro.  Water threatened 17 homes with 15-20 people being forced to evacuate. A 4 inch gas line was exposed near Stockyard and Alyssa Roads due to washout.
Road crews were required to remove mud, rocks and other debris that were pushed onto roads around the Mesquite area after up to 3.45 inches of rain fell.
Widespread street flooding over parts of east El Paso and Montana Vista.  Water was entering the home on Linda Rene St. in Montana Vista area.
An amateur radio operator had his east facing windows blown out of his house, and in same area a tractor trailer was overturned on Highway 11.
The aerostat balloon site measured a 61 mph wind gust.
Numerous large trees were blown down, two sheds blown over and a roof was blown off of a restaurant.
A wind gust blew a power line down in Lordsburg on South Main Street.
A wind gust was estimated at 60 mph along with low visibility from blowing dust.
Flash flooding was reported in Hatch.
A 58 mph wind gust was reported at the Santa Teresa Airport.

Emergency Operations Center was activated due to heavy rain and flash flooding in the Hatch area where 1.96 inches of rain was reported. About 40 people were evacuated from their residences in Hatch overnight.  Heavy equipment was necessary to shore up the banks of the Placitas and Rincon arroyos.  There was also a leaking gas main on NM 185.

NWS Storm survey revealed hundreds of ponderosa pines were either uprooted or snapped in the Village of Cloudcroft which resulted in damage to 30 structures, 10 vehicles and blocking 15 roads.  Prior to the damage occurring, light to moderate frozen precipitation fell which led to rime ice buildup on the windward side of exposed trees. Across the entire area, over 1000 trees were snapped or uprooted due to sustained winds of 60 to 70 mph through much of the day with gusts over 100 mph.  Cloudcroft lost power for over 24 hours starting around 11 am on 3/13. ||The most significant damage was located along a north to south exposed ridge line on the windward side of the mountain.
